additions.reason: Line 43 of the source text comments on the verse from Hoshea 4:6: 'נִדְמוּ עַמִּי מִבְּלִי הַדָּעַת'. The Rebbe writes: 'נִדְמוּ, הַיְנוּ כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה' — the word נִדְמוּ (they have perished / they have become like) IS a bechina of the koach ha-medame, the imagination. This is classic bechina language (הַיְנוּ). The word נִדְמוּ encapsulates the state of a person whose da'at has departed and who has fallen into the animalistic imagination — he has become 'nidam' (like a beast). This concept names the human condition-of-imagination-dominance directly from the verse, making it a distinct conceptual node.
additions.source_quote: נִדְמוּ עַמִּי מִבְּלִי הַדָּעַת — נִדְמוּ, הַיְנוּ כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה

additions.reason: Line 49 of the source text states: 'חֲלוֹם פַּרְעֹה אֶחָד הוּא — הַיְנוּ חֲלוֹם פַּרְעֹה... הוּא בָּא מֵאֶחָד, הַיְנוּ מֵאַהֲבָה, (כִּי אֶחָד הוּא בְּחִינַת אַהֲבָה, כַּמְבֹאָר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר). הַיְנוּ מֵאַהֲבָה נְפוּלָה כַּנַּ"ל'. The word אֶחָד is a bechina of אַהֲבָה (love), as taught elsewhere. In the evil imagination context, the dream of Pharaoh (= koach ha-medame) comes from 'אַהֲבָה נְפוּלָה' (fallen love) — the degraded love that results when da'at departs and the person falls to animal loves. This is an evil-polarity bechina: אֶחָד here = fallen love = the source energy of the evil imagination.
additions.source_quote: חֲלוֹם פַּרְעֹה אֶחָד הוּא... הוּא בָּא מֵאֶחָד, הַיְנוּ מֵאַהֲבָה, (כִּי אֶחָד הוּא בְּחִינַת אַהֲבָה, כַּמְבֹאָר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר). הַיְנוּ מֵאַהֲבָה נְפוּלָה כַּנַּ"ל

additions.reason: Lines 10 and 19 of the source text establish 'גָּדַלְתָּ מְאֹד' as a bechina of the specific practice of enlarging/measuring the mind (הַגְדָּלַת הַשֵּׂכֶל) in measured proportion. Together the phrase 'גָּדַלְתָּ מְאֹד' encodes the pairing of tefillin and tzitzit (expansion + contraction). This is bechina language establishing the scriptural phrase as a node.

additions.reason: Line 10 states: 'מְאֹד, שֶׁהוּא סִטְרָא דִּשְׂמָאלָא, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַצִּמְצוּם' — the word מְאֹד IS a bechina of the left side / tzimtzum. additions.reason: Line 21 states: 'תְּפִלָּה הִיא חַיֵּי שָׁעָה — הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת הָאָרֶץ הֲדֹם רַגְלָי הַנַּ"ל, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת רַגְלֵי הַקְּדֻשָּׁה הַמְלֻבָּשִׁין בְּזֶה הָעוֹלָם'. Flagging as borderline — the reviewer may want to add 'מִי עָלָה שָׁמַיִם וַיֵּרַד' as an explicit bechina node for the musician.

Line 72: 'שֶׁעִקַּר בְּחִינַת הָרוּחַ הוּא בַּיָּדַיִם, שֶׁשָּׁם פִּקְדוֹנוֹת הָרוּחוֹת'. The hands as the seat of spirits is context for why playing music with the hand gathers the good spirit.
